_README: TEMPLATE - every value below is an EXAMPLE. Do not copy ids into a real config.
The example project is a fictional 'Orion' so the shape is clear without implying
that any particular project is the one to watch.
Sibling state: state/<source>.json only - last_seen plus the last ~200 seen ids.

sources._hub: the resolved microsoft_* prefix for THIS install - resolve it, never assume
sources._max_results_note: Teams takes max_results; Slack takes limit. Small on purpose, and you PAGE rather than widen: one measured Slack read of 30 messages returned ~83k characters and errored outright rather than returning less.

sources._hub: the resolved slack_* prefix for THIS install
the estate whose credentials can see THIS repo - one source, one estate, never inferred
sources._branches_note: Default is the default branch ONLY. Watching every branch turns one merge into 40 items and buries the one commit that mattered.
sources._cursor_note: TWO cursors, kept apart: commits by committedDate, pulls by updatedAt. They advance independently and collapsing them loses whichever moves slower.
sources._dedup_note: A PR is long-lived and MUTABLE - it moves on every comment, label and transition. Dedup on <id>@<updatedAt>, never the bare id: the bare id reports a PR once and then never again, swallowing the merge you cared about. A commit is immutable, so its sha alone is enough.

sources.space_key: <the KEY, not the display title - titles get renamed, keys do not>
sources._cursor_note: page version.when (ISO-8601). Record version.number too: a typo fix and a rewritten runbook both bump it, and the report must say CREATED or UPDATED because only one of them usually needs an action.

sources._workspace_note: RESOLVE THE WORKSPACE/SITE ID LIVE EVERY RUN - never store it here. These are ephemeral: an estate's workspaces were recreated once and every hardcoded copy broke on the same day, in the boot doctrine and three notepads at once.
sources.board: <board id, OR omit and use project/person>

person._note: OPTIONAL - 'tickets related to this person'. ACCOUNT ID COMES FROM THE TRACKER'S OWN USER DIRECTORY, chosen by the operator from a list you printed. NEVER from a call you pass the identity to: such lookups have been measured IGNORING the id argument and returning the caller, so two of them 'confirm' each other and the report then silently covers the wrong human.
person.account_id: <picked by the operator from a directory search>
person.display_name: <shown at setup so the operator can confirm it is who they meant>

sources._cursor_note: issue updated (ISO-8601). Push it into the QUERY - `updated >= "<cursor>"` plus the board/person clause - and let the server filter. Pulling a whole board and filtering client-side turns one call into thirty.

_sources_note: A source is anything with an ordered stream and a cursor. Adding a kind means adding a row to the Source kinds table in SKILL.md - the check loop itself does not change. Non-chat kinds are HIGH VOLUME and their items are LARGE (a diff, a page, an issue body): keep ids, subjects and URLs, never the body, and expect report_max_items to actually bite - when it does, say how many were dropped and on what ordering.

orion._note: One block per project the operator named. Names as spoken AND as the system writes them. Read by a model judging relevance, not by a regex - so partial and fuzzy entries are useful here, not harmful.

identities._note: Re-read the posting identity IMMEDIATELY BEFORE EACH POST, not once at setup - it drifts. Measured: a Slack session reported one person's id early in a session and a different person's later in the SAME session, with nothing announcing the change. 'self' = ids to treat as our own output.

self: <the logged-in user id, read from the tool description this run>
slack._selffilter: NEVER put a colleague's id here. This list means 'ignore as my own output', so another person's id silently discards every message they post - for a listener watching their work, the worst failure this skill has.

_action_policy_note: The boundary is WRITES, not reads. report-only verifies freely (read tickets, logs, repos, cluster) and then reports and proposes; it just never writes. 'act' adds writes. Hard stops bind at both.
_report_note: Beyond this, give counts by topic and list the urgent ones plus the ones with a real action. A 60-item enumeration is unreadable anyway.
_sort_note: last_seen keeps each platform's NATIVE value (Teams ISO-8601, Slack epoch string). Those two are not comparable, so when ordering items from both in one report, sort on a normalised UTC timestamp computed for the sort only - and never write it back as last_seen.
